learningObjective: Reason about how a runtime decides where to place each op and tensor when the graph mixes CPU-only ops, GPU-native ops, and host↔device transfers.
stem: A model graph has some ops with only a CPU implementation and others with only a GPU implementation. Which of the following statements about device placement are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A device-placement pass typically inserts explicit host↔device transfer ops (e.g., MemcpyToHost / MemcpyToDevice) at boundaries between differently placed ops, and the emitted plan records those transfers so the runtime does not have to guess them.

Placing CPU-only ops on the GPU can be forced by the runtime by 'promoting' the CPU kernel implementation to a GPU kernel automatically; no additional lowering is needed because the runtime treats device tags as advisory hints only.
Alternating between CPU and GPU ops in the middle of a hot loop causes host↔device transfer traffic across PCIe/NVLink and can dominate the end-to-end latency, even if each individual kernel is fast.

Placement decisions should ideally minimize the total number of host↔device transitions along the critical path, sometimes at the cost of running an op on a slower device — the transfer cost can exceed the op-level savings.

explanation: Standard device-placement passes insert transfer ops at device boundaries (A). Alternating device execution introduces PCIe/NVLink transfer overhead that often dominates fine-grained ops (C). Consequently, placement heuristics minimize the number of device transitions on the hot path (D). Option (B) is false: 'device tags' are not advisory — an op with only a CPU implementation cannot be run on the GPU without providing a GPU kernel; the runtime cannot magically synthesize one.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: transfer-op insertion is standard in ONNX Runtime, XLA HloRunner, TensorRT (with explicit host tensors), and IREE.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: a CPU-only op needs a genuine GPU implementation to run on the GPU; there is no automatic 'promotion'.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: PCIe transfer cost is a well-known bottleneck for graphs with fine-grained device transitions.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: this is the standard placement heuristic (minimize crossings on the hot path).

assumptions: The runtime supports mixed CPU/GPU execution (typical of ONNX Runtime, XLA, IREE).
The graph is executed on a single machine with a distinct host and device memory space.
nonImplications: Does not imply that every CPU op must be moved to GPU; small ops on the CPU can be preferable to a round-trip.
Does not imply the runtime always uses PCIe; NVLink or unified memory may reduce but not eliminate transfer cost.
